prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map defines a checkout counter layout where the counter surface, cash register on the bottom left, and jar or paper bag on the far left sit nearest to the camera wearer at roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres (within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person across the counter). Directly in front of the camera wearer, a person stands behind the counter at about 1.0 to 1.3 metres away, flanked by the snack rack/bag ~0.4 metres to their right (viewer's left) and a heated display case and shelf unit ~0.8 to 1.0 metres to their left (viewer's right) at roughly 1.5 to 2.0 metres depth. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint tilts upward and slightly rightward so the foreground register drops out of the lower frame by frame 4 while the person's head enters the upper frame, and in frame 5 the person leans slightly forward as their left hand extends toward the counter edge to ~0.7 metres. The depth map makes the continuous 3D separation between the dark-jacketed torso, the foreground counter objects, and the recessed background hallway (3+ metres away) much clearer than in the low-contrast RGB image. However, it is unreliable inside the glass display case and open doorway where depth flattens to uniform black or flat grey, and along the thin held paper/card which merges into the hand and jacket surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete regions across the counter scene, consistently outlining the person standing ~1.0 to 1.3 metres in front of the camera wearer while their lower body remains occluded behind the foreground counter (~0.5 metres away). In frame 1, the person is on the upper left with their head cropped out of the top edge, a cash register directly below them on the counter is mislabelled as a 'laptop', a flat payment decal to its right is mislabelled as a 'remote', and a second person's hand at the far right counter edge (~0.5 metres away) goes completely unsegmented. Across frames 2 to 5, as the camera tilts up and pans right, the central person shifts from the upper-left to the centre-left and becomes visible from the waist up, while a jar on the left (~0.6 metres away, within arm's reach) is labelled 'cup' in frames 2–3 before being occluded by a foreground bag/coat miscategorized as a 'cat' in frame 4. Meanwhile, the display case ~1.5 to 2.0 metres away on the right enters view in frames 3–5 (labelled 'tv' with a 'bowl' on top and a 'cup' on the shelf below), and a stool behind the person (~2.2 metres away) is briefly segmented as a 'chair' in frame 2. While the masks clearly delineate object boundaries and silhouette shifts against clutter, the map is semantically unreliable—hallucinating labels like 'laptop', 'tv', 'cat', and 'cell phone' (on the held banknotes in frame 1) and missing the counter surface entirely.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks the upper-body and hand keypoints of the person standing ~1.0 to 1.3 metres across the counter, confirming they face directly toward the camera wearer with their torso frontal and both hands held within their own and the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.7 to 1.0 metres away) just above the counter. In frame 1, with the person's head cropped above the top frame edge, only two magenta hand skeletons are detected on the left: the person's right hand resting on the register (~0.6 metres away) and left hand holding bills (~0.9 metres away), while the extra hand at the far right edge is missed. In frames 2 and 3, while the head remains mostly out of view, detection degrades severely: frame 2 captures only the person's left hand in the lower-left foreground, and frame 3 produces an inverted, geometrically corrupted yellow torso skeleton in the upper centre with no hand keypoints. In frames 4 and 5, as the camera tilts up to reveal the head and shoulders, full yellow upper-body skeletons and facial keypoints appear, showing the person's head tilted downward so they look down toward their hands and the counter rather than into the camera, before extending their right arm downward to the left and their left hand forward in frame 5. The pose map precisely reveals finger articulation and downward head pitch through dark sunglasses in frames 4–5 that are hard to discern in RGB, but it is highly unreliable when the head is out of frame in frames 1–3 and never detects the lower body occluded behind the counter.
